solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like soldier from America clutching good spears

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so good goes within the soldier and America pieces

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An American soldier holds a set of good spears, as though armed for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The spears are not weapons: asparagus shoots are called spears.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus shoots are sold and served as spears, the green stems of the vegetable.

clue.text: A revolutionary green energy that's switched-on

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for green is read backwards

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A green-energy activist who is radical and alert to the issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks political here but means RAW, inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone switched-on is alert and well informed, so aware is a synonym.

clue.text: Curse those doing satire in the middle of stage

indicators.note: in the middle of means placed inside the phrase for stage

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it
satirists mock, so they are the mockers

explanation.surface: A satirical troupe swears loudly while standing centre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the mockers on' is a British idiom meaning to jinx something; 'in the middle of' splits the stage phrase between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the mockers on a plan is to jinx or spoil it, as if casting a curse.

clue.text: White queen that is given support

parts.note: R is short for regina, queen
a sling supports an injured arm

explanation.surface: The white queen in chess is propped up by another piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' sounds like a chess colour but is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a German grape and wine, almost always a white wine.

clue.text: Bringing up a beef gravy initially in need of stirring

indicators.note: in need of says the first piece wants the next one beside it
initially means the first letter of gravy is taken

parts.note: first letter of gravy
rousing means stirring, exciting

explanation.surface: A cook brings up beef and gravy that needs a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is not meat but a complaint, so bringing up a beef is grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Grousing is grumbling, raising a complaint, which in slang is a beef.

clue.text: Way to get a six-pack of drinks with vermouth in

indicators.note: in means the vermouth goes inside the word for drinks

parts.note: sups means drinks, sips
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a six-pack of drinks with vermouth among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The six-pack is stomach muscles, not cans. 'Gin and it' is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are an abdominal exercise that builds visible stomach muscles.

clue.text: Make a stink about showbiz magazine's twaddle

indicators.note: about means going around, so the smell word surrounds the magazine

parts.note: to hum is to smell bad
OK! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about the nonsense printed in a celebrity magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a stink' suggests complaining, but here it is HUM, to smell. OK! is a British celebrity magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokum is nonsense or claptrap, the same idea as twaddle.

clue.text: Complex way to end a call

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like an adjective but is the noun for an emotional problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a neurosis or inhibition; the phrasal verb names ending a telephone conversation.

clue.text: What convicts do after stealing, when job's done

indicators.note: after puts the convicts' piece after the stealing piece

parts.note: knocking off is slang for stealing
convicts do time in prison

explanation.surface: Criminals' career path: after a robbery, prison follows once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' suggests a robbery in the surface, but here it is ordinary work ending for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking-off time is the hour when workers stop for the day and go home.

clue.text: Person in movement stormed in furiously

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a protest movement storms in angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' sounds political but is an artistic movement, Modernism.
explanation.definitionFit: A modernist is a member of the Modernism artistic and literary movement.

clue.text: Periodically parroted European writer's style

indicators.note: periodically means every other letter is taken

parts.note: alternate letters of parroted
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A European writer's style is said to be echoed like a parrot now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of parroted, then the Italian author ECO.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: After tax returns, collapse several times

indicators.note: returns means the word goes back the other way

parts.note: net pay is what is left after tax
to fold is to collapse, as a business folds

explanation.surface: After filing tax returns, someone collapses repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax returns' looks like a single phrase, but 'After tax' is NET and returns tells you to reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenfold means ten times over, a multiplication of several times.

clue.text: The Spanish drinking your old kind of alcohol

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so el swallows thy

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A Spaniard drinks your old kind of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl alcohol, ethanol, is the alcohol found in drinks.

clue.text: Two different gulls or a woodpecker

parts.note: the clue wants two different words for gulls, dupes; the first is sap, a fool
a sucker is someone easily gulled, a dupe

explanation.surface: Two kinds of seagull are offered as the identity of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulls' are not seabirds but dupes, people easily fooled. 'Two' tells you there are two words for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapsuckers are a North American genus of woodpecker that feed on tree sap.

clue.text: Musing male in area covered by tiny bit of litter?

indicators.note: covered by means placed inside the word for the small animal

parts.note: the runt is the smallest animal in a litter

explanation.surface: A male animal lies pondering, buried under a scrap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish but means a brood of young. Ruminant also means a cud-chewing animal, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant as an adjective means contemplative, chewing things over in thought.

clue.text: Troops operational? Send in more of them

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British army troops
in force means in operation, effective

explanation.surface: Troops are deployed; an officer orders more of them sent in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on 'Troops' for its 'them'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen a position by sending extra soldiers.

clue.text: Opposing appeal North America backs

indicators.note: backs means goes backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: North America supports an appeal while others are against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like support but tells you to reverse IT and NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as an adjective or preposition means against, in opposition.

clue.text: Homemaker has fur tailored with lining of gold

indicators.note: with lining of means the gold goes inside the rearranged letters
tailored means altered and cut to shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A housewife owns a fur coat tailored and lined with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HAS FUR gives HSFRAU, and AU is inserted after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausfrau is German for housewife, a woman who runs the household.

clue.text: One's issue about oxygen, or about its forms?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pieces go round the oxygen symbol

parts.note: one is I, and 's is is, so One's gives IS
a topic is an issue under discussion
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemist's question: is oxygen the topic, or its various forms?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on oxygen: 'its forms' are oxygen's isotopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopic means relating to isotopes, the different atomic varieties of an element.

clue.text: Part of foot to squeeze, but not softly!

indicators.note: not says the soft letter is left out of the word for squeeze

parts.note: to pinch is to squeeze
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes part of a foot, but firmly rather than gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of foot' sounds anatomical but is a measure: twelve inches make a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is one twelfth of a foot in imperial length measurement.

clue.text: Travelling requirement in France not fun

parts.note: pas is French for not
sport means fun, as in good sport

explanation.surface: A traveller in France finds no fun in the paperwork needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the document needed to cross national borders.

clue.text: Tension from opening of secure lock

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of secure
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Tension builds from opening a secure lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is strain or pressure, mental or physical tension.

clue.text: Get lost with PC's routine using computers

parts.note: a police constable's regular patrol is the beat
IT is information technology, computing

explanation.surface: Someone tells the computer user to get lost with their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a personal computer but is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang command telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Speed of ships west of promontory

indicators.note: west of means to the left of, placed first in an across answer

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness names

explanation.surface: The speed of ships sailing west of a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetness is swiftness, the quality of moving quickly.

clue.text: Truly wanting both hands to fix paper in bunches

indicators.note: to fix means the paper is set inside the trimmed word
wanting means lacking, and both hands are right and left, R and L

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone truly lacks the hands to fix paper into bundles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both hands' are right and left, R and L; the FT, the Financial Times, is a British newspaper printed on pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufty describes hair or grass growing in tufts, clumps or bunches.

clue.text: Long period before November

indicators.note: before places the period first

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A long period of time before November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn, desire it strongly.

clue.text: Observe phantom, about to move forwards

indicators.note: to move forwards means the about piece shifts to the front of the word

parts.note: a spectre is a ghost or phantom
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Watch a ghost as it drifts forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: SPECTRE ends in RE; moving it to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect a rule or custom is to observe it, keep to it.

clue.text: Model car running around rubbish pile

indicators.note: around means the car letters surround the pile letters
running suggests movement and change, so car's letters are rearranged
rubbish as a verb or adjective signals the letters of pile are scrambled

explanation.surface: A model car runs round a heap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams here: 'running' works on car and 'rubbish' on pile, and the first wraps around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy or scale model of something.

clue.text: Dropping back, strayed around Irish town

indicators.note: around means turned round, read backwards
dropping back means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to stray morally is to sin, so strayed gives sinned

explanation.surface: Someone who strayed wanders back around an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNED loses its last letter D to give SINNE, which reversed is the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is the county town of County Clare in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Taste endless meal, but no starter, in club

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: to try food is to taste it

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter is dropped, a meal pun on first course

parts.note: a luncheon is a formal lunch

explanation.surface: A diner tastes a never-ending meal without a first course, at the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a dining club, but it is a weapon. 'Starter' plays on a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police officers.
